safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: No hazard analysis and risk assessment exists for foxBMS 2, and this is not one. The hazardous events belong to the fictional reference project this corpus declares; they are authored inputs of that project, and the record is in the corpus precisely so that the reference project's concept chain has a hazard to start from.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees artifact_type `hazard` with HE-01 at ASIL_D and ISO 26262 Part 3 and Part 4 Clause 6 mappings with status `mapped` will conclude a HARA was performed and returned an ASIL_D cell-overvoltage hazard. No HARA was performed for the product; these events and their S/E/C ratings are authored for a fictional project; and the mappings record which clause concepts the event shape was built from, not that a hazard analysis was carried out.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/application/soa/soa.c:81-146 (SOA_CheckVoltages) for the limit thresholds that make the hazard reachable; src/app/driver/afe/api/afe.h:124 (AFE_StartMeasurement) for the measurement the reaction chain depends on; https://iisb-foxbms.iisb.fraunhofer.de/foxbms/gen2/docs/html/latest/software/structure/software-structure.html (section anchor sw-structure, retrieved 2026-10-01) for the module structure. All at the pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437. The hazardous EVENTS have no external source: they originate in the fictional reference project.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source can detect the violation, and that a wrong measurement is a credible malfunctioning behaviour. It supports nothing about the events' severity, exposure, controllability or ASIL, all four of which are authored inputs of the reference project.

revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect this corrects is legibility, not content: this record was already honest in `origin: synthetic` and in revision prose, but a reader skimming `artifact_type` and `standards_mappings` would take hazard for something the foxBMS 2 project published and its ISO 26262 mapping for a claim of satisfaction. Neither is true, and the correction now says so in declarative fields on the record itself. derivation_basis names the file:line or the corpus record the derivation actually rests on, and states what it does not support, so a grader can check the derivation instead of taking it on trust. No other field of the record was modified.

malfunctioning_behavior: AFE reports incorrect cell voltage (stuck-at, drift, communication error) OR SOA fails to detect limit violation OR contactor fails to open on violation OR BMS fails to request contactor opening

hazardous_events.description: Cell overvoltage during charging leading to thermal runaway
hazardous_events.operational_situation: CHARGING mode, high SOC (>90%), fast charge (>1C), ambient > 45°C
hazardous_events.rationale: Thermal runaway can cause fire/explosion with fatal injuries; continuous exposure during charging; driver cannot detect or control individual cell overvoltage

hazardous_events.description: Cell undervoltage during discharge leading to copper shunts and potential thermal event on subsequent recharge
hazardous_events.operational_situation: NORMAL mode, deep discharge (<2.0V/cell), high load, low temperature
hazardous_events.rationale: Cell damage creates latent failure; moderate exposure during deep discharge; vehicle may provide warning but driver may ignore

safe_states: All HV contactors open (HV bus isolated from pack)
Fault logged to FRAM with timestamp and cell index
degraded_states: Balancing disabled for affected cell group
Enhanced monitoring: 1 Hz acquisition for affected cells
assumptions: Vehicle provides independent HW monitoring (e.g., redundant voltage monitor ASIL B)
Charger respects BMS charge current limits
Contactor opening is irreversible without service tool
FRAM retains fault data across power cycles
